strings.name: Alfonso Cuarón
strings.summary: Raised in Mexico City, Cuarón studied film and moved from television into features. Working between Mexican and English-language industries, he combines long takes, technical experimentation and social experience in Y tu mamá también, Children of Men, Gravity and Roma. Gravity and Roma brought two directing Oscars, and Disclaimer continued his exploration of television storytelling.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Connects technical experimentation and social memory in Gravity and Roma, advancing Mexican cinema’s international reach.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Technique and social memory
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses long takes and audiovisual technique to connect experience, class and history.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Transnational filmmaking
strings.highlights.h2.text: Expands storytelling and distribution across Mexican and English-language production.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Disclaimer

strings.timeline.t2.title: Roma at the Oscars
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won directing and cinematography; the film also won foreign-language feature.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Gravity at the Oscars
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won directing and shared editing with Mark Sanger.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Children of Men
strings.timeline.t4.text: Directed science fiction about migration, state violence and reproductive crisis.

strings.timeline.t6.title: Y tu mamá también
strings.timeline.t6.text: Co-wrote with brother Carlos, using a road story to portray Mexican society.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First feature
strings.timeline.t7.text: Released Sólo con tu pareja after television work.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Mexico City
strings.timeline.t8.text: Later studied film and gained experience in production and television.
